name: "Freezer Friendly" Cuban Black Beans with Bell Pepper, Cilantro & Lime (Batch-Cooking)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe makes about 16 cups of black beans or 8 (2-cup) servings.
TO SOAK THE BEANS: Place beans in a large pot and cover with cold water. Let soak for a minimum of 8 hours (or overnight) at room temperature.
Drain soaked beans, then return to the pot and cover with fresh water, making sure the beans are covered by at least 2 inches (adding more water to the pot if needed). Set aside.
TO COOK THE BEANS: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 red chili pepper
½ small bunch cilantro
1 lime

instructions.primary_message: Trim, seed, and quarter one of the bell peppers. Add to the pot with the beans, along with bay leaves. (Reserve remaining bell peppers for later use.)

Cover beans with a lid, then bring to a boil over high heat, skimming away any foam that rises to the surface. Once boiling, reduce heat to low and simmer (covered), stirring occasionally, until beans are tender and starting to split, about 1 ½ hours. (Do not drain the liquid).
FOR THE SOFFRITO BASE: Meanwhile, trim, seed, and small dice remaining bell peppers. Place in a medium bowl.

Quarter chili pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level. Mince and add to the bowl with the bell pepper. (Be careful with chilis; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel, halve, and small dice onions; peel and mince garlic. Add both to the bowl.
Preheat a large skillet over medium heat.

Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add bell pepper, chili pepper, onion, garlic, and spices; cook, stirring occasionally, until veggies are golden and soft, 8-10 minutes. Remove soffrito from heat and set aside until the beans are done.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tbsp neutral vegetable oil
2 tbsp cumin, ground
4 tsp oregano, dried
1 tbsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: When the beans are tender, uncover. Add soffrito and sugar to the pot, then stir to combine. Continue to cook (uncovered), stirring occasionally, until beans split and liquid has thickened, 35-40 minutes more. (For thicker beans, continue to simmer until beans are thickened to your liking. Additionally, the beans will continue to thicken as they cool.)
Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves.
When the beans are done, juice lime into the pot, add cilantro, and stir to combine. Set aside to cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally, about 30 minutes.
Once the beans have cooled to room temperature, divide between containers (discarding bay leaves and quartered bell pepper).

STORING: Cover each container with an air-tight lid (or wrap tightly with plastic wrap). Place in the freezer for up to 3 months. HEATING: For best results, thaw beans in the fridge overnight. Warm in a saucepan set over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until heated through, about 5 minutes.
